 June Jones, UH football’s winningest coach, dies
 By Stephen Tsai

 Star-Advertiser / 2003
 Hawaii coach June Jones consulted with quarterback Timmy Chang during a Hawaii Bowl game on Dec. 25, 2003.
 June Jones, who led the University of Hawaii to one of the greatest turnarounds in college football history, died today in Oregon.
 Jones, 73, had suffered health issues this year and entered hospice two weeks ago, according to a close family friend.
 A former UH quarterback in 1973 and 1974, Jones is the winningest coach in UH football history. He turned down an opportunity to be the San Diego Chargers head coach to accept the head coaching job at UH in December of 1998.
 After inheriting a program that finished 0-12 the season before, Jones led the Warriors to a 9-4 record and tied for first in the Western Athletic Conference. At the time, it was the greatest turnaround in college football history and earned Jones a National Coach of the Year honor.
 Under Jones, the Warriors went 12-0 in the 2007 regular season to win the WAC title and earn a berth in the Bowl Championship Series Sugar Bowl in 2008, losing to Georgia.
 After a contract dispute with UH, Jones left for SMU.

 He coached nine seasons at UH from 1999 to 2007 and earned 76 victories, while leading the Rainbow Warriors to six bowl games and three 10-plus win seasons. His teams won two WAC titles and he helped produce record-breaking quarterbacks such as Timmy Chang and Heisman Trophy finalist Colt Brennan.
 Jones was inducted into the Hawaii Circle of Honor in 2024.
